note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 65; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 18) on data/benches/salts_ph.json: salts' pH and an indicator's pKa by absorbance. A salt of a strong acid and a strong base is neutral; of a weak base's acid (NH4+) acidic; of a weak acid's base (acetate, carbonate) basic. An indicator is a weak acid whose two forms differ in colour: where both are present, Beer and Lambert's law gives their ratio, and the pH its pKa.
title: Experiment: salts' pH and an indicator's pKa

report.label: ammonium chloride's pH
report.why: Ammonium, the acid of the weak base ammonia (pKa 9.25), gives up a little of its hydrogen: in 0.1 M, pH = (9.25 - log10 0.1) / 2 = 5.1.

report.label: sodium carbonate's pH
report.why: Carbonate, the base of the weak acid hydrogen carbonate (pKa 10.33), takes hydrogen ions from water: in 0.1 M, pOH = (14.00 - 10.33 - log10 0.1) / 2 = 2.3, pH 11.6.

report.label: bromothymol blue's pKa
report.why: pKa = pH - log10([In2-] / [HIn-]), the ratio Beer and Lambert give: (A - A_acid) / (A_base - A) at 616 nm, where the blue form absorbs and the yellow hardly does. It is the apparent pKa at the buffer's ionic strength (about 0.1), 7.1, below the thermodynamic 7.5: the doubly charged blue form's activity is the lower.

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: Ammonium chloride is the salt of hydrochloric acid and the weak base ammonia. What pH do you expect for its 0.1 M solution? Type it, then click "predict".

steps.title: Their pH
steps.text: Right-click each beaker in turn and click "+ pH" under its readings: sodium chloride, ammonium chloride, sodium acetate, sodium hydrogen carbonate, sodium carbonate.
steps.why: A salt's ions are each an acid or a base, or neither: chloride and sodium are neither (their acid and base are strong); ammonium is a weak acid; acetate, hydrogen carbonate and carbonate weak bases, each by how weak its acid is.

steps.title: The spectrophotometer
steps.text: Pick up the spectrophotometer in Supplies and set it on the bench, at the right.

steps.title: 616 nm
steps.text: Right-click the spectrophotometer and drag its wavelength to 616 nm, where the blue form absorbs most.

steps.title: The blank
steps.text: Pick up the cuvette of water and click the spectrophotometer; then right-click it and click "blank".

steps.title: All yellow
steps.text: Take the water out and set it back on the bench; put the cuvette of the indicator in acid in the well. Right-click the spectrophotometer and click "+ A".

checks.text: the acid form in its well

steps.title: All blue
steps.text: Take it out and set it back; put the cuvette of the indicator in base in the well, and click "+ A".

checks.text: the base form in its well

steps.title: In the buffer
steps.text: Take it out and set it back; put the cuvette of the indicator in the phosphate buffer in the well, and click "+ A". Then right-click the cuvette and click "+ pH".
steps.why: Green: both forms. pKa = pH - log10((A - A_acid) / (A_base - A)).
